mechanism: Oral translational readthrough inducer; promotes near-cognate tRNA insertion at the premature UGA stop codon, allowing full-length BUBR1 translation
evidence_level: STRONG mechanism for UGA nonsense suppression; efficacy is allele/context-dependent (2–5% restoration reported in literature; ≥10% full-length BUBR1 is the Track 2 go/no-go threshold)
evidence_source: PMC5098639; Keeling et al. 2016; Welch et al. 2007
pediatric_status: FDA/EMA-approved for nonsense-mutation DMD (EU); pediatric dosing precedent in DMD and CF trials
risk_notes: Variable readthrough efficiency; may restore truncated protein that retains KEN/ABBA motifs; requires functional assay in patient cells
approved_jurisdiction: Brazil, Chile, Iceland, Israel, Korea, Liechtenstein, Norway, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Ukraine, United Kingdom (MHRA); not FDA or EMA

mechanism: Synthetic eukaryotic ribosome-selective glycoside (ERSG) that promotes UGA stop-codon readthrough
evidence_level: SUPPORTING in G542X CFTR PDOs/organoids; restores full-length CFTR protein and mRNA levels
evidence_source: ELX-02 Phase 2 NCT04135495; Eloxx 2020 Drug Future; JCF 2021
pediatric_status: Phase 2 completed in CF; no pediatric MVA data; subcutaneous/inhaled routes
risk_notes: Ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity class risk lower than aminoglycosides but not eliminated; requires patient-derived validation

mechanism: NAD+ precursor; SIRT2 deacetylation of BUBR1 K668 blocks ubiquitylation/proteasomal decay and raises BUBR1 protein in vivo
evidence_level: STRONG for protein rescue in mice/MEFs. Lifespan +58% (males +123%) is SIRT2-Tg in *BubR1^H/H*, NOT NMN
pediatric_status: GRAS supplement; adult trials ongoing; paediatric data limited
risk_notes: Low; theoretical NAD+ metabolism effects
approved_jurisdiction: none (dietary supplement / NDI; not an approved medication)

mechanism: Alternative NAD+ precursor on the same SIRT2/BUBR1 axis
evidence_level: SUPPORTING (same pathway; NR raises NAD+ in multiple tissues but was not the BUBR1 rescue arm)
evidence_source: Zhang et al. 2016 Science; North et al. 2014
risk_notes: Low
approved_jurisdiction: none (FDA GRAS no-questions for food use)

mechanism: Chemical chaperone and HDAC/proteostasis modulator; hydrolysed to phenylbutyric acid; rescues aneuploidy-associated neuronal apoptosis and protein aggregates in human iPSC models
evidence_level: SUPPORTING in human aneuploid iPSC neurons (trisomy 21/13); NO direct MVA/BUBR1 rescue data
evidence_source: Fisher et al. 2020 Sci Rep; Oromendia 2015; Ravicti FDA/EMA UCD approvals
pediatric_status: FDA-approved for urea-cycle disorders (including infants/children); sodium-free liquid; palatable
risk_notes: BBB/CNS penetration via MCT transporters; no sodium load; neurotoxicity at very high doses remains a theoretical risk; anti-proliferative effects are double-edged in a cancer-predisposed child

mechanism: Heat-shock response amplifier; stabilises lysosomal function; FDA-approved for Niemann-Pick C and crosses the BBB
evidence_level: SUPPORTING (paediatric approval; BBB penetration); NO direct MVA/BUBR1 rescue data
evidence_source: McKay et al. / Miplyffa FDA 2024; DailyMed SmPC
risk_notes: Theoretical risk: HSF1/HSP activation is an aneuploid-cancer survival pathway; could help aneuploid cells survive and expand; oncologic monitoring required
approved_jurisdiction: FDA (Miplyffa approved Sep 2024; EMA refused marketing authorisation Jul 2026)

mechanism: Disaccharide that induces mTORC1-independent TFEB nuclear translocation and autophagy-lysosome biogenesis; clears protein aggregates in neurodegenerative models; aneuploid cells activate TFEB due to lysosomal saturation
evidence_level: SUPPORTING in neurodegenerative storage (Batten) and aneuploidy lysosomal-stress models; NO direct MVA/BUBR1 rescue data
evidence_source: Santagouda & Amon 2015 Genes Dev; Sidransky et al. 2021; Settembre et al. 2011; DeBosch 2016 Sci Signal
pediatric_status: Food ingredient/GRAS; paediatric autophagy trials limited; high doses can cause osmotic diarrhoea
risk_notes: BBB penetration modest; does not address BUBR1 protein directly; Trehalase in gut limits oral bioavailability (forms exist to bypass this)

mechanism: Natural polyamine that promotes autophagy and TFEB activation through mTORC1-independent pathways
evidence_level: SUPPORTING in ageing/autophagy models; NO direct MVA/BBB/paediatric data
evidence_source: EBioMedicine/Eisenberg et al.; Morselli 2010 Autophagy
risk_notes: Bioavailability and CNS penetration uncertain; exogenous polyamine metabolism may alter cancer cell proliferation
approved_jurisdiction: none (EU novel food ingredient; no approved medication)

mechanism: mTORC1 inhibition; fly TOR-depletion / larval rapamycin rescued aneuploid neuroblast COUNTS (not brain size)
evidence_level: MODERATE in fly neuroblast count rescue; CAVEAT: unpublished *BubR1^H/H* mouse rapamycin diet negative (Baker 2013 Cell Rep note)
evidence_source: Gonzalez-Blanco et al. 2026 Nat Commun 17:3829; Sieben et al. 2020 JCI; Baker et al. 2013 Cell Rep 3:1164
risk_notes: Immunosuppression; growth delay; metabolic effects; infection risk — supportive only

mechanism: mTORC1 inhibitor; paediatric-approved for TSC-SEGA
evidence_level: SUPPORTING (same rapalog mechanism as sirolimus; less fly data)
evidence_source: EMBO Mol Med / clinical TSC literature; ChEMBL FKBP1A target
risk_notes: Immunosuppression; stomatitis; growth effects — supportive only

mechanism: Proposed pharmacological ROS scavenger on the fly Sod2/GTPx-1 axis (NAC was NOT the published fly intervention)
evidence_level: ANALOGUE only; fly brain-size rescue was Sod2 and GTPx-1 overexpression (Gonzalez-Blanco 2026); antioxidant supplements can promote metastasis in some cancer models
evidence_source: Gonzalez-Blanco et al. 2026 Nat Commun 17:3829; Piskounova et al. 2015 Nature 527:186-191; Sayin et al. 2014 Sci Transl Med 6:221ra15
risk_notes: Poor BBB penetration; potential pro-metastatic/anti-apoptotic effect in a cancer-predisposed MVA1 patient

mechanism: Mitochondria-targeted antioxidant proposed as pharmacological analogue of fly mito-chaperone / ROS-scavenger overexpression
evidence_level: ANALOGUE only; no direct MVA rescue data
evidence_source: Gonzalez-Blanco et al. 2026 Nat Commun 17:3829
pediatric_status: Supplement; phase 2 in other indications; paediatric data limited
risk_notes: Limited CNS data; does not address the primary BUBR1 defect

mechanism: Nrf2 activator -> antioxidant gene program (SOD2, GCLC, NQO1); ChEMBL screen hit for NFE2L2
evidence_level: SUPPORTING (approved for Friedreich ataxia; Nrf2 counteracts aneuploidy-driven ROS); CAVEAT: Nrf2 activation can promote chemoresistance and tumour survival
evidence_source: Lynch et al. 2021 Lancet Neurol (MOXIe); ChEMBL CHEMBL1075094
pediatric_status: FDA-approved (Friedreich ataxia 2023); adolescent data in FA trials
risk_notes: Transaminitis; fatigue; theoretical oncogenic risk in established aneuploid clones

mechanism: Approved tyrosine-kinase inhibitor for Ph+ CML and ALL; used as the approved component of a dasatinib + quercetin senolytic adjunct
evidence_level: SUPPORTING in vivo mouse (adjunct only)
evidence_source: Baker et al. 2011 Nature 479:232-6
pediatric_status: FDA-approved for Ph+ CML and Ph+ ALL in children >=1 year
risk_notes: Myelosuppression; infection; QT effects; senescent-cell clearance may alter tumour microenvironment unpredictably; use only as an oncology-supervised adjunct

mechanism: Flavonoid dietary supplement; the non-approved, supplement component of the dasatinib + quercetin senolytic adjunct
evidence_level: ANALOGUE only
evidence_source: Baker et al. 2011 Nature 479:232-6 (dasatinib + quercetin combination in BubR1H/H mice)
risk_notes: Myelosuppression; infection; QT effects; senescent-cell clearance may alter tumour microenvironment unpredictably; not an approved drug; use only as an adjunct

mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibition suppresses type-I IFN downstream of micronuclei->cGAS-STING; paediatric compassionate-use in AGS/CANDLE/SAVI
evidence_level: STRONG paediatric clinical evidence in interferonopathies (adjunct; biomarker-guided)
evidence_source: NEJM 2020 (35 AGS patients); JCI 2018 (Montealegre Sanchez); ChEMBL JAK1/JAK2 hits
risk_notes: Infection; lymphopenia; thrombosis; **potential impairment of NK/tumour surveillance in a cancer-prone MVA1 child**

mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor; approved paediatric GVHD; case evidence in SAVI/AGS
evidence_level: SUPPORTING (paediatric approvals + case reports)
evidence_source: Frontiers Pediatr 2021; ChEMBL JAK1/JAK2 hits
risk_notes: Infection; cytopenias; **tumour-surveillance caveat**

mechanism: Anti-IL-6R; CIN cells depend on cGAS-STING->IL-6/STAT3 survival; reduces CIN-driven inflammation
evidence_level: SUPPORTING (CIN biology; paediatric-approved)
evidence_source: Hong et al. 2022 Nature 607:366-73; ChEMBL CHEMBL1237022
risk_notes: Infection; infusion reactions; **tumour-surveillance caveat**

mechanism: SAC override -> premature anaphase -> MORE aneuploidy; cancer-killing strategy
evidence_level: WRONG DIRECTION for BUB1B hypomorphism
evidence_source: CFI-402257 PNAS 2017; BOS172722 ICR 2020; ChEMBL CHEMBL3983
risk_notes: Would worsen disease

mechanism: Error-correction kinase inhibition -> more mis-segregation
evidence_level: WRONG DIRECTION
evidence_source: ChEMBL CHEMBL2185
risk_notes: Would worsen disease

mechanism: Amplifies micronuclei-driven IFN cascade
evidence_level: WRONG DIRECTION
evidence_source: ChEMBL CHEMBL4523377
risk_notes: Would worsen neuroinflammation
